title: In Situ TEM Probing of Structural and Electronic Dynamics of Nanoparticles for Energy Materials
content: Nanoparticles play a crucial role in energy-related applications, including catalysis, solid oxide fuel cells, and photovoltaic systems, as well as in other fields such as sensor technologies and biomedical applications [1-3]. Their high surface-to-volume ratio results in a significant fraction of atoms being exposed at the surface, leading to enhanced interactions due to the increased number of active sites. However, several key questions remain regarding characterization and its impact on nanoparticle functionality, such as defect chemistry, gas-solid interaction-driven surface rearrangements at high spatiotemporal resolution, and charge redistribution under light illumination. To address these challenges, a suite of techniques based on aberration-corrected high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (AC-HRTEM), integrated with in situ capabilities, was developed and applied to visualize and characterize dynamic phenomena.
